description: Welcome to Rasheed FieldShift! We are tackling "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data" right here in Azare. Our goal is to build an easy-to-use web tool combining NASA climate and soil moisture data with local farming knowledge to help farmers compare smart crop-rotation strategies. Looking for 3–5 teammates in Azare: web/frontend developers, Python/data analysts, UI/UX designers, and agriculture researchers/presenters. All skill levels welcome!
summary:
Rasheed FieldShift is a web-based agricultural decision-support project designed to help rain-fed smallholder farmers understand seasonal environmental conditions and explore crop-rotation options. Its initial pilot focuses on Azare, Bauchi State, Nigeria.

The project integrates NASA Earth-observation and climate information, including rainfall and temperature data from NASA POWER, with locally relevant agricultural knowledge. It presents environmental summaries, visual trends, and comparisons of candidate crop rotations, helping users understand potential opportunities, risks, and uncertainties.

FieldShift addresses the challenge of making better-informed farming decisions in regions where rainfall variability and limited access to environmental information can affect agricultural planning. By making scientific data easier to understand and highlighting the importance of local validation, the project aims to support more informed conversations among farmers, agricultural extension workers, and researchers.
details:
Project Overview

Rasheed FieldShift is an agricultural decision-support web application developed to help rain-fed smallholder farmers explore environmental conditions and compare potential crop-rotation strategies.

The initial pilot focuses on Azare, Katagum Local Government Area, Bauchi State, Nigeria.

How It Works

The application is designed around four core functions:

  1. Location-based environmental information: Users can explore environmental conditions for a selected location, beginning with Azare.
  2. Climate analysis: NASA POWER rainfall and temperature information is processed into understandable summaries and visual trends.
  3. Crop-rotation comparison: Users can compare candidate crop sequences, including continuous millet, millet–cowpea–sorghum, and groundnut–sorghum–sesame.
  4. Decision support: The application presents environmental context, assumptions, possible risks, and information that requires local agricultural validation.

Benefits and Intended Impact

FieldShift aims to make environmental information more accessible to farmers and agricultural stakeholders. It can support seasonal planning, improve understanding of rainfall patterns, and encourage evidence-informed discussions about crop rotations.

The long-term goal is to support more informed agricultural decisions and strengthen the ability of farming communities to respond to environmental variability.

Technologies Used

  • Frontend: Next.js, React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS.
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI, and Uvicorn.
  • Data processing: Pandas and NumPy.
  • Data retrieval: NASA POWER API.
  • Development tools: Git and GitHub.

Creativity and Innovation

FieldShift connects environmental data with practical agricultural decision-making. Rather than simply displaying climate information, it aims to help users interpret that information alongside crop choices and rotation scenarios.

The project emphasizes transparency by communicating data sources, units, spatial limitations, missing information, and uncertainty.

Important Consideration

Crop-rotation scenarios are exploratory hypotheses, not guaranteed recommendations. Local agronomic research, extension guidance, and farmer knowledge are necessary before making specific recommendations. NASA gridded environmental data is not a direct measurement of an individual farm.
